The tenderer's personal data may be registered in the Early Detection and Exclusion System (EDES) 
if the tenderer is in one of the situations mentioned in Article 136 of the Financial Regulation9. For 
more information, see the privacy statement: 
http://ec.europa.eu/budget/explained/management/protecting/protect_en.cfm. 
5. Means of redress. 
Tenderers may submit any observations concerning the procurement procedure to the contracting 
authority using the contact details under Heading I.1 of the contract notice. If tenderers believe that 
there is maladministration, they may lodge a complaint to the European Ombudsman within two 
years of the date from which they become aware of the facts which form the basis for the complaint 
(see https://www.ombudsman.europa.eu).   
Within two months of notification of the outcome of the procedure (award decision), tenderers may 
launch an action for its annulment. Any request tenderers may make and any reply from the 
contracting authority, or any complaint for maladministration, will have neither the purpose nor the 
effect of suspending the time-limit for launching an action for annulment nor open a new period for 
launching an action for annulment. The body responsible for hearing annulment procedures is 
indicated under Heading VI.4.1 of the contract notice.  
 
Yours faithfully, 
Juhan Lepassaar, Executive Director 
 (e-signed)
